subject: Hosted metering: input/output/tool tokens and rounding — examples and next steps
body:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@acme.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying hosted metering for upcoming SOW

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question as we finalize the SOW: we need a plain-language explanation of how Redwood will meter tokens for hosted API calls in three edge cases so our procurement/finance folks can sign off. Our questions are specifically:

1) Bulk ingest + single generate: we call /generate once per document batch (10k documents total), prompt includes a 300-token system+instruction prefix and each generated result averages 120 tokens. Are system tokens charged on the request or only on the model? Is rounding done per-batch or per-request?

2) Retrieval + tool calls: we use a retrieval tool that returns 2,400 tokens of context, then call the model which streams a 6,000-token output. How are the retriever "tool" tokens attributed (input vs output)? If a streaming response is interrupted, how is rounding/proration handled?

3) Multi-step tool chains: we make a chain where an internal tool calls the model multiple times within one outer HTTP request (three separate model calls). Do we bill each internal model call separately (i.e., rounding three times) or is there a single aggregation?

Also: how do committed-use discounts apply against per-token rounding? For example, if hosted list price is $0.0008/input and $0.0012/output and we have a committed discount of 18% on hosted usage, at what point is the discount applied (per-call after rounding, or on aggregated monthly totals)?

Appreciate a succinct breakdown and a couple of numeric examples we can paste into the finance review. If helpful, feel free to attach a CSV with worked examples.

Thanks,
Jared
Procurement — Acme Corp

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jared Cole <jared.cole@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying hosted metering for upcoming SOW

Hi all — quick (worked) examples below. Marissa/Monica, please correct my wording if I mix billing/legal terms.

Summary of primary rules (short):
- Tokens billed = input_tokens + output_tokens + system/tool_tokens (all rounded up to the nearest whole token).
- Rounding granularity: rounding occurs per model invocation. If your client code issues three separate model calls (even in a single HTTP wrapper), we bill each model call separately (i.e., rounding happens on each call).
- Tool / retriever tokens: tokens emitted by a tool that are passed into the model as context are counted as input tokens. If the model itself invokes a tool and that tool returns content after the model call, that content is usually counted as output tokens attributable to the model call that produced them.
- Streaming: tokens are billed as produced. For interrupted streams, we bill tokens that were emitted by the model before termination (rounded per token as produced). No additional rounding-up after stream close other than per-token whole counts.
- Discounts: committed-use discounts are applied to the billed usage (post-rounding) on a monthly aggregation basis (i.e., we apply discount against the summed billed tokens for the month for hosted API usage).

Worked examples (numbers simplified):
1) Bulk ingest + single generate (single model call per batch):
- System + instruction prefix: 300 tokens (input)
- User prompt / batch payload: 1,200 tokens total across the batch (input)
- Model output (generated): 120 tokens per document * 10k docs = 1,200,000 tokens (output)
- Billing: input = 300 + 1,200 = 1,500 tokens; output = 1,200,000 tokens; total = 1,201,500 tokens. Rounding happens at each model call, but since this is one call per document batch the rounding effect is minimal compared to volume.
- Example cost (hosted list): input @ $0.0008/token, output @ $0.0012/token => pre-discount = (1,500 * 0.0008) + (1,200,000 * 0.0012) ≈ $1.20 + $1,440 = $1,441.20.

2) Retrieval + streaming (retriever returns 2,400 tokens, model streams 6,000 tokens):
- Retriever output passed into model = 2,400 tokens (counted as input)
- System/instruction: 150 tokens (input)
- Output streamed: 6,000 tokens (output), billed as emitted tokens
- Billing: input = 2,400 + 150 = 2,550; output = 6,000; total = 8,550 tokens.
- If the stream is interrupted after 1,800 tokens emitted, billed output = 1,800 (no additional rounding plusses beyond whole tokens).

3) Multi-step tool chain (three separate model calls inside single outer request):
- Because each model call is a separate model invocation, we bill each call separately. So if each call's inputs+outputs round up slightly, those rounding deltas can add up for small, frequent calls.
- Example: three calls with totals (call1=135 tokens, call2=142 tokens, call3=158 tokens) => total billed = 135 + 142 + 158 = 435 tokens (each was rounded on its own).

Discount application example:
- Using scenario #1 above, monthly billed tokens after rounding → cost pre-discount $1,441.20. If Acme has an 18% hosted discount applied to hosted API monthly usage, the discount is applied to the $1,441.20 producing $1,183.78 net. That is, discount applies to the aggregated billed amount for the month for hosted API usage.

Marissa / Monica — please attach the formal CSV and confirm the per-model-call rounding language and any special-cases for streaming/proration.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — adding formalized language and attachments. Key bullets for contract language (copy-paste friendly):
- Metering: Redwood bills for the sum of (input_tokens + output_tokens + system/tool_tokens). All token quantities are integer counts; fractional tokens are not billed.
- Attribution: Tokens that are provided to the model as part of the request payload (including retriever/tool context) are counted as input_tokens. Tokens produced by the model (including content produced as the result of tool invocation initiated by the model) are counted as output_tokens. System messages (the model/system/instruction role content you set) are counted as input_tokens.
- Rounding: Billing rounding is applied at the model invocation level: each model call’s token counts are rounded to the nearest whole token (effectively rounded up since we bill whole tokens). There is no monthly-level rounding; rounding is done before monthly aggregation.
- Streaming: Tokens are billed as produced. If a stream is terminated partway, the customer is billed for tokens emitted prior to termination.
- Discounts and commits: Committed-use discounts for hosted API are applied to the aggregated monthly billed amount for hosted usage after rounding. Committed discounts do not change how rounding is applied — they apply against the billable amount.

Attachments included: ratecard_v3.pdf (hosted list rates and published discounts), token-counting-examples.csv (CSV with the three worked scenarios above and line-item token math).

Note: for very small, highly chatty patterns (lots of subcalls), customers may see an effective overhead from per-call rounding; we can model alternatives (e.g., batching recommendations or recommending a dedicated capacity commit) if that overhead matters.

Jared — happy to put this language in the SOW. Ben, can you confirm whether an 18% hosted discount is within our committed discount bands for Acme's expected volumes or if we should propose a 15% standard tier + another commercial concession?

—Marissa
Billing Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: ratecard_v3.pdf (application/pdf), token-counting-examples.csv (text/csv)
